title: TS SDK: type factories for discriminated structured outputs and zod/json-schema adapters
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The TypeScript SDK currently supports structured output helpers (existing Zod-based helpers) but has recurring gaps when users try to: 1) return discriminated unions from model structured outputs, 2) validate partially streamed payloads during long responses, and 3) keep generated type helpers in sync with both Zod and JSON-Schema consumers.

Problem statement: Teams building product features want first-class ergonomics for: (a) type-safe discriminated unions produced from structured model output, (b) Zod validators and JSON-Schema artifacts generated from the same source of truth, and (c) a streaming-safe validator/parser that can be used to incrementally validate and recover from transient parse/retry errors. Current helper utilities are scattered and brittle when combined with streaming and retry semantics.

Goals:
- Provide a deterministic TypeFactory codegen that emits TypeScript types + Zod schemas + JSON-Schema for structured output specs.
- Add a small runtime for streaming-aware parsing: incrementally build and validate discriminated unions as tokens arrive, surfacing partial validation errors and restart points to the caller to support safe retries.
- Surface ergonomic helpers in the SDK: createZodFromOutputSchema(), exportJsonSchema(), and parseStreamingStructuredOutput().
- Ship concise examples and migration guide for existing Zod helpers.

Non-goals: Automatic model editing or speculative transforms of model output; experimental runtime-only validation (we do not replace backend eval infra).
acceptance_criteria: TypeFactory codegen produces: a) TypeScript types, b) corresponding Zod schemas, and c) JSON-Schema artifacts from a single structured-output spec file.
Generated discriminated unions compile cleanly in a TS project and narrow correctly in typical TypeScript control flow (switch by discriminator, if-checks, etc.).

parseStreamingStructuredOutput(stream, schema) can accept partial token batches and either return a partial validated object or a well-documented error with a stable resume token position for retries.
SDK exposes createZodFromOutputSchema and exportJsonSchema helpers with tests and examples in examples/structured-output and docs/snippets.
Backward-compatibility: existing users of the previous Zod helper can upgrade with a migration guide and unit-tested shim for the top 3 common idioms.
Perf: typegen and schema generation must run as part of the normal codegen pipeline without >10% increase in runtime for typical model specs (benchmark against a 12-field schema).
design_notes:
TypeFactory approach: we will treat the structured-output spec as the single source of truth. The codegen will emit three artifacts for each spec: .d.ts types, a zod schema factory (Z.function(() => schema)) that is lazy-safe for circular shapes, and JSON-Schema (Draft-07-compatible) with a top-level $id. Discriminator handling: require the spec to declare a discriminator field name (default 'type') and per-variant schemas. The generated TypeScript union will carry a literal discriminator type (e.g., { type: 'User' } | { type: 'Error' }). Runtime validators: Zod schemas will embed refine checks for cross-field invariants where provided. Streaming parser: parseStreamingStructuredOutput will accept an async iterable of string tokens (or chunk objects), accumulate into a buffer, and attempt incremental JSON extraction using a small state machine (depth counter + last-complete-object position). On successful partial parse, call zodSchema.safeParse to validate; if validation fails due to missing tail tokens, return state 'incomplete' with resume position. On validation failure due to type mismatch, return 'reject' with error and include top-level mismatch path. Retry semantics: SDK will expose a resumeToken (byte offset index of token stream) and a helper resumeFromToken that the caller can supply when replaying from Redwood API retry hooks.

API sketches:
- createZodFromOutputSchema(specString | json): ZodSchema
- exportJsonSchema(specFile): string (json-schema)
- generateTsArtifacts(specPath): writes .d.ts + zod factory + .schema.json
- parseStreamingStructuredOutput(stream, zodSchema, opts?): { status: 'complete'|'incomplete'|'invalid', value?: any, resumeToken?: string, errors?: any }
implementation_steps: 1) Add TypeFactory codegen module to ts-sdk: parser for structured-output spec format (YAML/JSON).
2) Implement Zod schema factory emitter with support for discriminators and lazy() to handle recursion.
3) Implement JSON-Schema exporter with $defs for shared shapes and discriminator mapping using oneOf/anyOf as appropriate.
4) Build parseStreamingStructuredOutput runtime: token accumulator, incremental JSON detector, zod safeParse integration, resume token generation.
5) Add TypeScript type declarations (.d.ts) generator that uses literal discriminator unions for better narrowing ergonomics.
6) Write unit tests for typegen output (compile tests), zod runtime validation, JSON-Schema compliance, and streaming parser edge cases.

7) Create example repo snippets and two end-to-end examples in examples/structured-output: a) chatbot responses that return union types for 'reply'|'tool'|'error', b) batch embeddings metadata with discriminated items.
8) Docs: migration guide, API reference, and a short RFC-style doc describing retry/resume semantics for streaming structured output.
9) Code review and security sign-off if necessary; performance benchmark and fix any hotspots.
10) Ship behind feature flag, opt-in beta, gather telemetrics, then flip on by default in sdk-ts-0.19.0.
Estimated PRs: ~4 (codegen core, runtime parser, examples/docs, tests/compile-checks).
examples: // Resume example: caller receives an 'incomplete' with resumeToken and calls API with Range header + resumeToken to continue streaming parsing.
qa_plan: Unit tests for codegen output identical to snapshot fixtures (d.ts + zod.rs + json-schema).
Compile-time tests: run tsc on a consumer fixture that imports generated .d.ts and exercises narrowing.
Integration test: spin up a small mock model that emits a truncated JSON object mid-stream; ensure parseStreamingStructuredOutput returns 'incomplete' and can resume correctly.
Fuzz tests: feed malformed token sequences and confirm SDK never throws uncaught exceptions (always returns structured error).
Performance test: compare codegen runtime on 100 specs baseline vs new generator; acceptance if <10% regression.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind 'structuredOutputTypegen' flag in SDK config for initial beta users.
Invite 10 internal teams to test examples and provide migration feedback (2-week window).
Monitor error rates and resume success rate in telemetry for 2 weeks after default flip.
After stability window, promote to GA in sdk-ts-0.19.0 release notes with migration guide.
notes: Trade-offs: Keeping a single source-of-truth makes codegen simpler but requires consumers to adopt spec-first workflow.
We debated emitting Ajv validators instead of Zod; chose Zod for developer ergonomics and better TypeScript inference.
Open question: whether resumeToken should be byte-offset or token-index; implementation uses token-index for initial launch to avoid byte encoding ambiguities.
